The **fiber** package provides three [S7](https://rconsortium.github.io/S7/)
classes for representing diffusion MRI tractography data in R:

| Class        | Represents                                            |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| `streamline` | A single fibre tract (a polyline of 3-D points).      |
| `bundle`     | A collection of streamlines (a tractogram / bundle).  |
| `bundle_set` | A collection of bundles (white-matter bundles of a subject, or across subjects / sessions). |

Together they let you store geometry, per-point and per-streamline attributes
(e.g. fractional anisotropy), and per-bundle or per-set metadata, and they
come with a concise set of tools for computing shape descriptors, resampling
onto uniform grids, computing the Hausdorff distance, and coercing to and from
the `dwiFiber` S4 class of the
[dti](https://cran.r-project.org/package=dti) package.

This vignette walks through the core workflow. A companion, technical
[vignette](fiber-api.qmd) (`fiber-api`) describes the complete API in detail.

## Loading fiber

```{r}
#| label: setup
if (!requireNamespace("fiber", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # R CMD check re-builds vignette outputs in a fresh R process where the
  # just-installed package is not always on the library path (seen on Windows).
  # Skip the executable chunks rather than fail the build in that case.
  knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
} else {
  library(fiber)
}
```

## Building a streamline

A `streamline` stores a `$P \times 3$` matrix of coordinates. The columns must
be named `"X"`, `"Y"`, and `"Z"`.

```{r}
# A helix in 3-D, sampled at 50 points
t <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 50)
sl <- streamline(
  points = cbind(X = cos(t), Y = sin(t), Z = t / (2 * pi))
)
sl
```

You can attach per-point attributes (e.g. fractional anisotropy) via
`point_data` and per-streamline scalars (e.g. a mean FA or a label) via
`streamline_data`:

```{r}
sl <- streamline(
  points = cbind(X = cos(t), Y = sin(t), Z = t / (2 * pi)),
  point_data = list(FA = runif(50)),
  streamline_data = list(mean_FA = mean(runif(50)), label = "helix")
)
sl@n_points            # 50
sl@point_attributes    # "FA"
sl@streamline_attributes  # c("mean_FA", "label")
```

## Shape descriptors

Functions like `get_curvilinear_length()`, `get_sinuosity()`, and
`get_euclidean_length()` compute scalar shape descriptors from the geometry:

```{r}
get_curvilinear_length(sl)
get_sinuosity(sl)
```

`get_curvature()` and `get_torsion()` return a per-point profile along the
arc-length abscissa:

```{r}
head(get_curvature(sl))
```

`add_shape_descriptors()` attaches several descriptors to an object at once.
Scalar descriptors land in `@streamline_data`; per-point ones (`curvature`,
`torsion`) land in `@point_data`:

```{r}
sl2 <- add_shape_descriptors(sl)
sl2@streamline_data$euclidean_length
head(sl2@point_data$curvature)
```

## Bundling streamlines

Wrap a list of `streamline`s in a `bundle`. Any `@streamline_data` keys common
to **all** streamlines are lifted automatically into `bundle@streamline_data`
as length-`S` vectors:

```{r}
sl_a <- streamline(points = cbind(X = cos(t), Y = sin(t), Z = t / (2 * pi)))
sl_b <- streamline(
  points = cbind(X = 1.1 * cos(t), Y = 1.1 * sin(t), Z = t / (2 * pi))
)
b <- bundle(streamlines = list(sl_a, sl_b))
b
b@n_streamlines                 # 2
b@streamline_data$mean_FA       # lifted automatically, if present
```

You can mix streamlines and bundles with `bind_bundles()`:

```{r}
b2 <- bind_bundles(sl_a, b)
b2@n_streamlines  # 3
```

## Reparametrisation

`reparametrize()` resamples streamlines onto a uniform arc-length grid using
linear interpolation. A single streamline can be resampled to any number of
points; by default a `bundle` is resampled to the rounded mean number of
points across its streamlines:

```{r}
sl_20 <- reparametrize(sl_a, n_points = 20L)
sl_20@n_points  # 20

b_20 <- reparametrize(b, n_points = 20L)
b_20[[1]]@n_points  # 20
b_20[[2]]@n_points  # 20
```

## Hausdorff distance

`compute_hausdorff_distance()` computes the symmetric Hausdorff distance
between streamlines. Depending on the inputs, it returns a scalar, a vector,
or a `dist` object:

```{r}
# streamlines -> scalar
compute_hausdorff_distance(sl_a, sl_b)

# bundle (with no second argument) -> pairwise dist object
d <- compute_hausdorff_distance(b)
as.matrix(d)

# bundle vs streamline -> vector
compute_hausdorff_distance(b, sl_a)
```

The core pairwise computation runs in C++ (via cpp11) for speed.

## Bundle sets

A `bundle_set` collects `bundle` objects. Two use cases are equally well
supported: grouping the multiple white-matter bundles of a single subject, or
grouping bundles across subjects / sessions. Names of the input list (like
`"callosum"` or `"sub-01"`) are transferred into `bundle_set@bundle_data` as the
`id_from_input_names` attribute:

```{r}
# Single subject: several white-matter bundles of one subject
bs_single <- bundle_set(list(callosum = bundle(list(sl_a)),
                             arcuate  = bundle(list(sl_b))))
bs_single
bs_single@n_bundles          # 2
bs_single[["callosum"]]      # extract one bundle (push-down)

# Multi-subject: the same bundle across two subjects / sessions
b_sub01 <- bundle(streamlines = list(sl_a), bundle_data = list(subject = "sub-01"))
b_sub02 <- bundle(streamlines = list(sl_b), bundle_data = list(subject = "sub-02"))

bs <- bundle_set(list("sub-01" = b_sub01, "sub-02" = b_sub02))
bs
bs@bundle_data$subject       # c("sub-01", "sub-02")
bs[["sub-01"]]               # extract one subject (push-down)
```

`bundle_set` objects also support `reparametrize()` and
`add_shape_descriptors()`, which operate per bundle and preserve
`@bundle_data` / `@bundle_set_data`.

## Interoperability with the dti package

If the [dti](https://cran.r-project.org/package=dti) package is installed, you
can coerce fiber objects to and from its `dwiFiber` S4 class:

```{r}
if (requireNamespace("dti", quietly = TRUE)) {
  dfi <- as_dwifiber(b)
  class(dfi)          # "dwiFiber"
  b_back <- as_bundle(dfi)
  b_back@n_streamlines
}
```

`as_dwifiber()` uses per-point directions stored in `@point_data`
(`direction_x`, `direction_y`, `direction_z`) when present, otherwise it
estimates them from the coordinates via finite differences.
